column_semantics: For bank debt, the schedule has a Spread above Index column and an Interest Rate column; when PIK appears, it is attached to the printed spread (for example, S+ 725 PIK) while the Interest Rate column shows the resulting stated current rate. For preferred equity, the Interest Rate column prints the PIK rate directly (for example, 10.00 % PIK). The filing does not present separate cash and PIK rate columns or a separate additive PIK percentage on top of the stated rate.

rationale: The printed schedule marks PIK within the stated rate/spread text itself. Loan rows show a single current Interest Rate computed from the printed index spread, with PIK attached to that spread rather than a separate numeric PIK rate. Preferred equity rows print one Interest Rate value followed by PIK. Because no separate Cash/Paid-in-Kind columns or additive separate PIK percentages are printed, the stated position-level rate is the all-in stated coupon/rate with PIK included where marked.
